A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViTime and RealTS research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices I–IV support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot forecasting, fine-tuning, rescaling, and model-configuration experiments in Tables I–II, Figures 4–5, and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional fine-tuning outcomes for Electricity, Traffic, and Weather.

M1.justification: The RealTS generator, binary-image mappings, Visual Time Tokenizer, Decoder, Refining Module, preprocessing, and training objective remain unchanged. The expanded abstract describes existing components.

E1.justification: Reported fine-tuning coverage expands from the four ETT datasets to include Electricity, Traffic, and Weather in Tables II, A.2, and A.3. This is a limited extension within the existing seven-dataset suite; all three already appeared in zero-shot evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched experiments. PatchTST, SiMBA, and TIMESNET already appeared in v1; v2 extends their comparisons to additional fine-tuning datasets. TimesFM, GPT4TS, and TIME-LLM entries for those added datasets are marked Not Reported.

E3.justification: The stated configurations and evaluation procedures are retained. Added fine-tuning results use the existing 10%/100% data proportions and forecasting horizons of 96, 192, 336, and 720; no revised splits, metrics, or training budgets are documented.

E4.justification: The rescaling analysis in Figure 4, resolution/lookback/model-size ablations in Figure 5, and illustrative forecasts in Appendix III are unchanged. The added appendix entries are benchmark results, not new diagnostic analyses.

E5.justification: The existing error bars and shaded bands in Figures 4–5 are unchanged. v2 introduces no additional run or seed information, uncertainty-reporting practice, or significance procedure.

E6.justification: Tables II, A.2, and A.3 add fine-tuning results for three datasets while retaining all earlier numerical entries. For example, newly reported ViTime 10% averages are 0.252, 0.254, and 0.252 for Electricity, Traffic, and Weather. Some additions are inconsistent: Traffic at 100% is 0.279 in Table II but averages 0.250 in Table A.3.

T1.justification: Definition 1, the synthesis distributions, mapping equations, training objective, rescaled-error definitions, and Appendix I distributions are mathematically unchanged. No proofs or formal results are added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a visual foundation model, RealTS synthetic training, strong zero-shot forecasting, and data-efficient fine-tuning. The abstract adds methodological explanation without changing these contributions or their claimed scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning visual processing, possible data leakage under rescaling, and configuration tradeoffs remain unchanged. The additional fine-tuning results receive no new substantive interpretation or limitation discussion.

D1.justification: Sections 3.6 and 4.1 and Appendices I–II retain the same normalization, synthetic-data settings, model dimensions, default hyperparameters, and architecture details. Code-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 24 references and related-work discussion are retained, including SiMBA and TIMESNET. Positioning against numerical foundation models and earlier visual forecasting work does not substantively change.

P1.justification: The abstract gains an explanation of RealTS and temporal-to-spatial mapping, and the introduction receives limited wording edits. Jingdong Chen is added to the author list, affiliations are removed, and the Appendix A.3 model label is shortened. Section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table II gains three dataset columns, and Tables A.2–A.3 gain dataset blocks, placing A.3 on a separate page. Figure 2 is split across two pages through reflow. Existing figure content, axes, and plotted results remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added horizon-level fine-tuning results strengthen evidence for data efficiency beyond the ETT family, and the abstract explains the method more clearly. These are limited gains, tempered by reporting errors: Traffic at 100% is 0.279 in Table II versus 0.250 in Table A.3, and TIMESNET's Weather average is reported as 0.267 although its four entries average 0.2865. The detailed results remain useful, but these inconsistencies weaken reporting reliability.
